Inspect table metadata and options

Source: R/frontend.R
tosi_metadata.Rd

These functions return information about a table, not observation rows. tosi_metadata() describes the subject and source. tosi_schema() describes the structure, including the components and their available domains. Use the same source_filter and aggregation with tosi_schema() as for the planned data request.

tosi_aggregation_options() lists source-provided choices where supported. Look for TRUE in the aggregation_options column of the connector listing from tosi(). tosi_data_version() checks the version reported by the connector independently of retrieval.

Usage

tosi_schema(path, source_filter = NULL, aggregation = NULL, lang = NULL)

tosi_metadata(path, lang = NULL)

tosi_aggregation_options(path, lang = NULL)

tosi_data_version(path)

Arguments

path

A data path beginning with a connector ID and /, followed by a canonical object ID or a supported source identifier or path. Use the object_path returned by catalogs and searches directly for retrieval and inspection.

source_filter

Optional selection of source values, series, or rows to retrieve. The accepted format and defaults depend on the connector. See tosi_help() for connector-specific instructions.

aggregation

Optional named list selecting source classifications or aggregation levels by dimension. On connectors that support it, use tosi_aggregation_options(path) to inspect available choices. See tosi_help() for connector-specific instructions and examples.

lang

Optional explicit result language. A non-NULL value overrides the session preference for that call.

Value

  • tosi_metadata(): a TosiMetadata object, which may include TosiSourceReference cards.

  • tosi_schema(): a TosiSchema object.

  • tosi_aggregation_options(): a named list of available aggregation choices grouped by source dimension.

  • tosi_data_version(): a POSIXct timestamp named by the canonical object path. It is not necessarily an uncached check and does not pin a later retrieval. For the version actually delivered, use the schema attached to the returned table.

See also

tosi_data() for retrieval and tosi_help() for available connector-specific selection instructions.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# After setting up a trusted connection (see ?tosi_options):
path <- "eurostat/sdg_07_40"
metadata <- tosi_metadata(path, lang = "en")
metadata$print(details = TRUE)
schema <- tosi_schema(path, lang = "en")
schema$components
tosi_data_version(path)
} # }
